historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Thiazide and thiazide-like diuretics

starting.description: An earlier report of sulfanilamide-associated diuresis and acidemia supplied background for carbonic-anhydrase-inhibitor research, according to a later review. In Beyer's directed salt-excreting programme, a carboxyl-substituted synthetic sulfanilamide analogue yielded chloride excretion; Beyer identifies this observed lead as the reason for more work on saluretic sulfonamides, culminating in chlorothiazide.

inspiration.description: Renal salt and water physiology informed the therapeutic objective; observations of sulfanilamide-associated diuresis and of a synthetic analogue's chloride-excreting effect supplied background and a specific working lead, respectively.

steps.description: A later review traces the research background to an observed diuretic effect and acidemia with sulfanilamide and subsequent carbonic anhydrase work. Beyer's team sought a practical oral agent to promote salt and water excretion, guided by physiological reasoning and comparative renal testing.
A carboxyl-substituted sulfanilamide analogue caused chloride excretion, strengthening the work on saluretic sulfonamides.

Structure–activity research in that line culminated in chlorothiazide; the original chemistry report describes synthesizing the benzothiadiazine series and their saluretic effects, and subsequent work included hydrochlorothiazide.

The family came to include thiazides such as bendroflumethiazide and hydrochlorothiazide and structurally diverse thiazide-like sulfonamides such as chlorthalidone and indapamide, which lack the benzothiadiazine ring; a review summarizes their development together without supplying each programme's founding steps.

In a distinct thiazide-like example, a 1961 clinical study identified chlorthalidone as a Geigy sulphonyl benzophenone derivative and described a longer-acting sodium- and chloride-excreting response similar to chlorothiazide; this is evidence of the established branch, not its founding rationale.

design.description: Researchers set a salt-excretion objective, made and compared sulfanilamide analogues, measured renal responses, and developed the saluretic lead into sulfamylbenzothiadiazine structures including chlorothiazide and related thiazides.

circumstances.description: Beyer describes a deliberate programme seeking salt excretion. A later review calls the earlier sulfanilamide observation accidental and the chloride-versus-bicarbonate effect of chlorothiazide unexpected. The exact expectations at each experimental stage are not resolved by these differing accounts.

limits: Beyer's direct account concerns the chlorothiazide programme; the class review describes thiazide-like compounds but does not establish separate chlorthalidone or indapamide founding paths.

The 1961 chlorthalidone paper is a clinical evaluation after synthesis, not a discoverer account of its founding research motivation. Similar excretory action does not establish an identical founding path.
conflicts: Beyer characterizes the chlorothiazide programme as planned work aimed at sodium chloride excretion and reports an earlier chloride-excreting analogue; Ernst and Fravel describe chlorothiazide's chloride rather than bicarbonate excretion as unexpected. The accounts differ in emphasis and possibly in which researchers' expectations or experimental stages they describe; they do not establish exactly what was anticipated at each step.

Beyer's 1977 retrospective says chlorothiazide was marketed in 1957; Ernst and Fravel's 2022 review says launched in 1958. Different definitions or jurisdictions are possible, but the discrepancy has not been resolved and is not needed for the origin classification.
gaps: The original Novello–Sprague 1957 paper was located but not read; only the displayed opening page of the distinct 1960 original was read.
The 1937 sulfanilamide report cited by the 2022 review was not read; the early observation is attributed to that review rather than represented as direct reading of the original.
Primary founding sources for the structurally distinct thiazide-like compounds, including the 1959 synthesis cited by the chlorthalidone clinical investigators, have not been read.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Clinical diuresis and acid-base effects of sulfanilamide helped motivate the carbonic-anhydrase and later saluretic programs.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The link is retrospective and the 1937 original was not read; immediate chlorothiazide development also depended on dog experiments.
